relay.title: Feed relay
relay.example: Each feed will be fetched as {{request}}
relay.empty: Empty — this browser can read only the feeds that allow it, which is almost none
relay.notice: This is a browser, so publishers’ feeds cannot be read directly — they are on other sites and those sites do not allow it. Until you supply a relay, the bulletin is a bundled demonstration: made-up stories from made-up newsrooms, so that the app has something to show. A relay is a machine that fetches real feeds on the app’s behalf. It therefore sees every feed asked for, which is a record of what you read, so use one you run or one you would trust with that. No relay is supplied and none is recommended. The desktop app needs none of this.

ai.notice: AI assistance is optional and never load-bearing. With it switched off, or with a provider that will not answer, the bulletin is written by the station's own templates exactly as it is now. The key you save is kept on this device — the operating system's credential store on the desktop, encrypted storage in a browser — and is sent to the provider you choose and to nobody else. What that provider charges is billed to your account.

device.title: On this device
device.description: Your settings, the caches behind them, which stories have already been read — and, if you switched them on, crash reports.

key.title: Your API key
key.description: In the operating system keychain, never in a settings export, and never read back to the screen.

leaves.title: What leaves it
leaves.description: Only the requests your settings ask for: the sources you ticked, and any service you switched on.

welcome.title: Welcome to your news channel
welcome.body: This is a television station that reads the day’s real news. It gathers stories from newsrooms you choose, decides which one leads, writes the bulletin and puts an anchor in front of a camera to read it. Three of those decisions are yours, and this is where they are.

sources.title: The news comes from newsrooms you pick
sources.body: Nothing here writes the news. Every story is somebody else’s journalism, credited on screen and linked back to the newsroom that filed it. Open News Sources to tick a country, a language or a single publisher — or to add a feed of your own.

relay.title: In a browser, you are watching a demonstration
relay.body: A web page is not allowed to read another site’s news feed, so this build cannot reach a real newsroom on its own. Until you point it at a relay under News Sources, the bulletin you are watching is an authored demonstration — the badge in the corner says so. The desktop app has no such limit.

anchor.title: Somebody has to read it
anchor.body: The anchor is a character with a voice, chosen on the Anchor screen. Voices range from the one your device already has to a downloadable one that sounds like a broadcaster. Anchors are content, not code: a folder dropped into your packs directory turns up on that list.

era.title: And a television to watch it on
era.body: An era is not a set or a graphics package — it is the television. Pick 1968 and the picture arrives in monochrome through a shadow mask; pick 1994 and it comes off a worn tape. The Picture screen holds the seven of them, and how hard the set is allowed to work.

finish.title: That is the whole of it
finish.body: Everything else is on the menu, which opens with Escape, the Menu button on a remote or Start on a controller. You can read this again whenever you like — there is a row for it on the System screen.

fault.title: The app stopped
fault.body: Something in the interface failed and the broadcast could not carry on. Your settings and your sources are unaffected.
